picks.name: CeeDee Lamb
picks.rationale: 83% for 40+. The clear alpha with 17 targets (44 yards, then 153) in the highest-total game on the board (53.5), with Dallas a 3-point underdog, so the passing volume should be there. He had a minor ankle issue this week (missed Wednesday, full on Friday) and is active. The soft Rio field is the other flag.

picks.name: Chris Olave
picks.rationale: 82% for 40+. He's the whole Saints passing game so far: 23 targets, 182 yards and then 86. The Raiders secondary is thin today (safeties Stukes and Dalton Johnson and corner Luter are all inactive), and WR3 Barion Brown is out, which concentrates targets. The catch is that the Saints' rookie left tackle is out against Maxx Crosby, so expect quicker throws.

picks.name: Ashton Jeanty
picks.rationale: 85% for 40+. A true workhorse: 44 carries in two games (102 and 48 yards), with only token work for Mike Washington, and he cleared 40 even in his bad week. New Orleans is allowing 5.0 yards a carry, and it's a dome. The one worry is the Saints as 3.5-point favorites forcing the Raiders to throw late.

picks.name: Derrick Henry
picks.rationale: 90% for 50+ on the ground. He has cleared it both weeks (144 yards on 24 carries, then 68 on 16), and Dallas is giving up 173.5 rushing yards a game with starting linebacker Overshown out. Risks: Justice Hill's growing snap share, a backup left tackle making his first start, more Lamar keepers, and a patched-up Maracana field that passed Friday's inspection but is still soft. 90% leaves room even after the early-season haircut.

picks.name: Lamar Jackson
picks.rationale: 81% for 175+. He threw for 324 and 235, and the Dallas secondary is gutted (Hooker, Durant and Locke all out). Left tackle Ronnie Stanley is inactive, though, which confirms the model's line alert. Add a staff emphasizing QB runs and Zay Flowers on a pitch count, and it's a B.

picks.name: Tyler Shough
picks.rationale: 82% for 175+. He leads the NFL with 662 passing yards and New Orleans throws a ton, in a dome. The concern is protection: first-round left tackle Kelvin Banks is out, and his backup draws Crosby against a Raiders front tied for the league lead in sacks.

picks.name: Dak Prescott
picks.rationale: 74% for 200+. This game has a 53.5 total, Dallas's defense is short four starters so Baltimore should score, and Dak threw for 279 last week. Week 1's 175 in a loss to the Giants shows the floor risk, so B.

picks.name: Mike Evans
picks.rationale: 88% for 25+. San Francisco's receiver room is gutted (Robinson, Pearsall and Kirk all on IR), so Evans should see plenty of targets. He was questionable with a hip and left last week's game early, though, so there's early-exit risk. He's active.

picks.name: Trey McBride
picks.rationale: 81% for 40+. He has 23 targets in two games (95 yards, then 41) and Arizona should be chasing as a 7.5-point underdog, which means volume. We hold at B because San Francisco has allowed just 175 passing yards a game and Brissett threw for only 95 last week.

picks.name: Brock Bowers
picks.rationale: 89% for 25+, but that assumes a normal workload. This is his season debut after a knee scope, and he may be on a snap count. Watch list only.

picks.name: George Kittle
picks.rationale: 71% for 25+. With three receivers on IR he should see more targets, and his snaps are climbing back from the Achilles (80 yards last week after 12 in Week 1). Still a ramp-up, so watch list.

picks.name: Justin Jefferson
picks.rationale: 69% for 40+. Kyler Murray's return should open up a passing game that Wentz kept short, and Tampa's pass defense has struggled. Only 15 targets through two games, so we're watching rather than betting.

picks.name: Aaron Jones
picks.rationale: 76% for 40+ on the board, but we downgraded. Jordan Mason is on IR, yet Minnesota's coaches have said they want to manage Jones's knee (he finished Week 2 in a brace), starting center Nick Samac is out, Kyler Murray's return should mean more passing, and Tampa allows just 3.0 yards a carry. In Week 1 he got 12 carries for exactly 40. Watch list.

passes.name: Zay Flowers
passes.reason: The board loves him (83% for 40+ receiving) because it simulates a full workload, but he's coming off a hamstring and is reportedly on a 20-30 snap pitch count on a soggy field. Not a bet.

passes.name: Travis Etienne Jr.
passes.reason: 92% for 25+ rushing on the board, but the Saints backfield is a three-way split with Kamara and Kendre Miller active, against a strong Raiders run defense. Early-season rule: no unsettled backfields.

passes.name: Bucky Irving
passes.reason: 80% for 40+ rushing, but Tampa put him on a pitch count and says it will ride the hot hand, against a Vikings run defense allowing 3.0 yards a carry.

passes.name: Jordan Mason
passes.reason: On IR (thumb surgery), but the board still simulates him (78% for 25+ rushing). Not playing.

passes.name: James Conner
passes.reason: On IR (foot); the board's 79% for 25+ rushing assumes he plays.

passes.name: Brandon Aiyuk
passes.reason: The board shows 83% for 25+ receiving off prior usage, but he hasn't played in 2026 and isn't among the 49ers receivers reported active today. Not a bet.

passes.name: Ricky Pearsall / Christian Kirk
passes.reason: Both are on IR; their board rows assume they play.
